findings.description: The RDS instance explicitly sets `storage_encrypted = false`, leaving database storage and automated storage artifacts unencrypted at rest. Compromise of underlying storage or snapshots can expose database contents.

The MySQL parameter group does not set `require_secure_transport = ON`. The application user data also connects with `mysqli_connect` without TLS options, so database credentials and application data may traverse the network in cleartext.

This rule permits all protocols and ports to `0.0.0.0/0` from the database security group. A compromised database or an abused database-side capability could initiate unrestricted external connections, defeating network egress segmentation.

The EC2 role grants every S3, EC2, and RDS action against every resource. Any compromise of an instance using this profile yields broad cloud control and data-access capabilities far beyond those required for a database web application.

User data embeds the database password in a generated PHP configuration file. EC2 user data is available through the instance metadata service to processes with instance access and is retained in Terraform state/launch configuration, unnecessarily broadening exposure of the database credential.

No `metadata_options` block requires IMDSv2, so the EC2 default permits IMDSv1. A server-side request forgery or local process compromise could retrieve the instance-profile credentials without IMDSv2's session-token protection.
